title: The Hotel Investment Lifecycle Is No Longer Linear, According to New Cushman & Wakefield Insight
summary: Higher capital costs, operational complexity and shifting investor expectations are forcing hotel owners to rethink decisions at every stage of ownership.
body_markdown:
The Hotel Investment Lifecycle Is No Longer Linear


*Higher capital costs, operational complexity and shifting investor expectations are forcing hotel owners and developers to revisit decisions at every stage of ownership*


[NEW YORK](https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/en/united-states/offices/new-york) – Cushman & Wakefield today published[The Hotel Investment Lifecycle Is No Longer Linear](https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/en/united-states/insights/hotel-investment-lifecycle-is-no-longer-linear) , a new insight article by Preston Puleo, MAI, Executive Director and National Advisory Co-Lead for Hospitality & Leisure, Valuation & Advisory. The article examines how higher capital costs, operational complexity and shifting investor expectations are reshaping hospitality real estate decisions from acquisition through disposition.


“The hotel investment lifecycle is no longer linear,” said[Puleo](https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/en/united-states/people/preston-puleo) . “The traditional sequence of planning, development or acquisition, operations and disposition increasingly resembles a continuous cycle of strategic decision-making. Owners are revisiting underwriting assumptions, evaluating exit strategies years before a sale and reassessing financing structures long after closing.”


There are three forces driving the shift. First, capital is more expensive and more selective, with projects increasingly advancing on a differentiating advantage such as an attractive basis, a compelling redevelopment opportunity, public incentives, strong sponsorship, a difficult-to-replicate location or meaningful operational upside. Second, operational performance is driving a greater share of value creation as ownership periods lengthen and investors revisit assumptions more frequently. Third, exit strategy now begins at acquisition, as brand selection, management agreements, capital structure and design decisions shape the future buyer pool and refinancing options.


Puleo notes that early decisions can carry long-term consequences. A branding decision made during pre-development can influence construction costs, financing availability, operating margins, future capital requirements and the universe of potential buyers at disposition, while management agreements can limit flexibility long after original assumptions have changed.


Once a hotel opens, the article observes, asset managers increasingly serve not only as performance monitors but as strategic advisors on refinancing, capital planning, renovation strategy and management-company accountability. It adds that the strongest dispositions are rarely the product of a marketing process alone, but the culmination of years of disciplined planning and execution.


“Disposition is not simply an event. It is the outcome of every major decision that preceded it,” Puleo said.


To read the full article, click[here](https://www.cushmanwakefield.com/en/united-states/insights/hotel-investment-lifecycle-is-no-longer-linear) .
